\section[der Wald]{der Wald — a forest}

\label{lesson:GE-C83-wald}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the German for a leaf; a sheet of paper, then the German for a mountain.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: der Wald}
\textbf{der Wald} — \textquotedblleft{}a forest\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{Wald} $\leftarrow$ Old High German \emph{wald} $\leftarrow$ Proto-Germanic \emph{*walþuz}, \textquotedblleft{}high land covered with wood\textquotedblright{} — inherited. (EtymDB 2.1) English \emph{wold}, as in the Cotswolds, is the same word.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{der Wald}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{der Wald}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{der Wald}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the German for a leaf; a sheet of paper, then the German for a mountain, then say \emph{der Wald} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does der Wald mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A forest\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
